Evan (People Ops): welcome Sam T :wave: quick security checklist for new joiners: 1) Security Essentials course 2) enroll device in Intune MDM 3) enable disk encryption (BitLocker) 4) set up 2FA (authenticator or YubiKey). Phishing sim for new hires will run next Mon 10:00am PT. Links: https://training.redwood.com/security-essentials and https://mdm.redwood.com/enroll. DM IT Helpdesk for enrollment issues.

Sam T: thanks! i'm on a corp-win laptop and i see BitLocker is "Off". IT asked me to enable it but i'm worried about losing access to my files if something goes wrong. Any tips?

Riley - InfoSec: good catch. For Windows we require BitLocker ON for corp devices. Before turning it on, create a BitLocker recovery key backup to your corporate OneDrive (recommended) or print it. Steps: open Control Panel -> System and Security -> BitLocker Drive Encryption -> Turn on BitLocker, follow prompts. Or run `manage-bde -on C:` as admin. If you run into issues, IT Helpdesk can remote assist and preserve the recovery key.

IT Helpdesk: @Sam T if you want, we can push BitLocker via Intune and escrow the recovery key to Azure AD automatically. Send your machine hostname and we'll check. Also make sure TPM is enabled in firmware — some older devices need TPM turned on in BIOS/UEFI for BitLocker auto-provisioning.

Sam T: ah ok. also saw a note about phishing sims — are those ever SMS-based? i use my personal phone for 2FA codes and don't want to get a fake text and click it.

Riley - InfoSec: currently our new-hire phishing sims are email-only. We do run occasional SMS/voice tests for high-risk cohorts but those are opt-in and clearly communicated. For phone-based 2FA we recommend an authenticator app or hardware key vs SMS. If you see any suspicious texts, forward them to security@redwood.com.

Sam T: another quick one — my partner sometimes uses my laptop to check email. Is that allowed?

Riley - InfoSec: short answer: no for company-managed laptops. Company devices must be used only by the assigned employee. For BYOD there are similar constraints if you're enrolled — avoid sharing access. If you need a secondary account or a guest session, ask IT and People Ops and we'll discuss options.

IT Helpdesk: For Intune enrollment on Win: 1) open Settings -> Accounts -> Access work or school -> Connect 2) sign in with SSO and accept device management 3) post-enroll, confirm policy: run `dsregcmd /status` and check MDM status. If enrollment fails, send a screenshot and `systeminfo` output.

security-bot: Course assigned -> Sam T: "Security Essentials" (course id: 514). Due: 2026-04-01.

Sam T: thanks all — i'll DM hostname and start the training now. Appreciate the BIOS tip about TPM.

Evan (People Ops): perfect, ping us if anything blocks setup. We'll keep the phishing sim window limited to new joiners only.
